title: Stripe Payments vs Stripe Managed Payments
summary: Two modes in the Stripe ecosystem with different legal sellers, responsibilities, eligibility, checkout rules, and total fees.
recommendation: Use ordinary Stripe Payments when you want to remain the merchant and own the operating stack. Consider Managed Payments for eligible digital transactions where transferring indirect-tax, fraud, dispute, and transaction-support responsibility justifies the added fee and product-eligibility limits.

differences.second: Link is presented as Merchant of Record for the managed transaction.
differences.whyItMatters: This is a responsibility change, not a Stripe settings shortcut.

differences.first: Payment-method pricing, such as 2.9% + $0.30 for US domestic cards.
differences.second: Adds 3.5% per successful Managed Payments transaction to Payments fees.
differences.whyItMatters: Compare the combined amount, not 3.5% against 2.9%.

differences.first: Generally available in Stripe-supported business locations.
differences.second: Generally available in Stripe's documented Managed Payments business locations (39 seller countries as of the 2026-04-22 GA changelog, including Australia).
differences.whyItMatters: Seller country and product eligibility must still be procurement gates.

differences.first: Broad eligible online goods and services.
differences.second: Eligible digital products; services, physical goods, platforms, and multiple categories are prohibited.
differences.whyItMatters: Many ordinary Stripe businesses are not eligible for Managed Payments.

differences.first: Your merchant identity and configured Stripe checkout experience.
differences.second: Sold through Link, standardized transaction emails, and Link order support.
differences.whyItMatters: Brand, support, receipts, statements, and customer expectations change.

implementation.summary: Managed Payments reduces tax, fraud, dispute, and transaction-support operations, but it is not the lowest-code Stripe path. Ordinary Payments can start with a no-code link; Managed Payments requires a Checkout Session and deliberately removes several advanced integration choices.

first.label: No code
first.detail: Ordinary Stripe Payments supports dashboard-created Payment Links for one-time and recurring sales.

second.label: Low code
second.detail: Managed Payments supports hosted or embedded Checkout Sessions and Payment Links for eligible digital products.

first.label: Broad choice
first.detail: Payment Links, Checkout, Elements, mobile SDKs, and PaymentIntents cover low-code through advanced flows.

second.label: Narrower choice
second.detail: Checkout and Payment Links are supported surfaces; Connect platforms and several advanced flows remain excluded.

first.label: Existing mode
first.detail: No Managed Payments-specific flags, eligibility checks, or Link seller presentation are required.

second.label: Checkout update
second.detail: An eligible Checkout integration is updated to enable Managed Payments and supply supported product tax codes.

first.label: Stripe Billing
first.detail: The full compatible Billing surface is available, with merchant-owned webhook and access logic.

second.label: Billing with limits
second.detail: Subscriptions use Stripe Billing through Managed Payments Checkout, with restrictions on invoice items and off-cycle invoices.

first.label: Merchant managed
first.detail: The merchant owns tax registrations and filings, disputes, fraud decisions, and transaction support.

second.label: Link managed
second.detail: Link handles covered indirect taxes, fraud, disputes, transaction support, and standardized transaction emails.

first.label: Stripe toolkit
first.detail: Sandboxes, CLI, SDKs, Workbench, test clocks, and integration-specific documentation.

second.label: Same core toolkit
second.detail: Uses Stripe's Checkout and Billing tooling, plus Managed Payments eligibility and behavior constraints.

first.label: Merchant branded
first.detail: The merchant identity anchors checkout, receipts, statements, support, and configured payment methods.

second.label: Standardized by Link
second.detail: Checkout says sold through Link; Link owns payment terms, transaction emails, and transaction-level support.

first.label: Maximum flexibility
first.detail: More integration paths and product types are available, with more responsibility retained by the merchant.

second.label: Fewer decisions
second.detail: A narrower eligible product and integration surface reduces choices but can simplify covered operations after launch.

scenarios.when: You already use Checkout for eligible digital products and want MoR only in selected markets.
scenarios.reason: Transaction-level enablement is its distinctive advantage.

scenarios.when: You need Elements, platforms, physical goods, services, or maximum billing flexibility.
scenarios.reason: Managed Payments eligibility and integration limits are material.

scenarios.when: Your seller country or product category is outside Managed Payments eligibility.
scenarios.reason: Managed Payments remains limited to documented business locations and eligible digital products.
